Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh rate paired with a 40 fps cap gives a smooth, tear-free experience that suits the game's cinematic pacing; medium textures and shadows look noticeably better than low without overwhelming the GPU. Keep HairWorks and ray tracing off — they are disproportionately expensive on RDNA 2.

profiles.Summary: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered is a demanding open-world RPG that pushes the Steam Deck's RDNA 2 GPU hard, particularly in dense areas like cities and during heavy combat; expect 30–45 fps depending on settings. With FSR upscaling and tuned in-game settings it runs well enough to be enjoyable, though the remastered ray-tracing features must be avoided entirely on Deck hardware.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the remastered PC minimum requirements (GTX 1660 class, well above the Deck's ~GTX 1050 Ti GPU) and general Deck hardware capability. On your first run, check the frame-rate counter in a busy outdoor area like Novigrad and drop to Max Battery settings if the Optimal profile dips below 35 fps consistently.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 1280x800 keeps the GPU well within the 8 W TDP budget; image quality is soft but perfectly playable for long sessions. All ray-tracing and high-cost effects are disabled to preserve battery.

KnownIssues: Ray tracing options (if exposed) will tank performance and must be disabled on Deck hardware.
Dense areas like Novigrad city can cause significant frame-rate drops even at low settings.
The remastered version's higher base GPU requirements mean the Deck sits below minimum spec; expect occasional stutters during shader compilation early on.
Some UI text and menus may appear small at 1280x800 — use the Adjustable Text Size accessibility feature to compensate.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Running at full 15 W TDP with the GPU at max clock extracts the best the Deck can realistically offer; the frame rate will hold 40–45 fps in most open-world areas but may dip into the mid-30s in Novigrad. Battery life is short — best used plugged in or for shorter play sessions.

Optimal.Notes: Medium textures and SSAO give a noticeably better image than Max Battery with manageable GPU cost; the 30 fps cap holds well in open wilderness and most quest areas, with rare dips in Novigrad. This is the recommended daily-driver profile for most players.

profiles.Summary: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered is a demanding open-world RPG whose PC minimum GPU (GTX 1660) sits well above the Steam Deck's roughly GTX 1050 Ti-class RDNA 2 GPU, making it a challenging title that requires careful settings tuning, FSR upscaling, and TDP management to achieve playable frame rates. With low-to-medium settings and FSR the Deck can maintain a stable 30 fps in most areas, though dense locations like Novigrad and heavy combat scenes will stress the hardware significantly.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements versus the Deck's hardware class. On first run, check frame rate in Novigrad (the hardest area) and drop to Max Battery if it falls below 25 fps consistently.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with Deck FSR upscaling keeps GPU load low enough for the 8 W TDP cap to hold 30 fps in most areas; expect occasional dips to ~25 fps in Novigrad. Half-rate shading is left off as it produces visible artifacts in this title's lighting model.

KnownIssues: Novigrad and other dense urban areas can cause significant frame drops even at low settings due to CPU and GPU bottlenecks on the Deck's Zen 2 / 8-CU RDNA 2 hardware.
The next-gen remastered version adds ray tracing and enhanced foliage that are not viable on Deck — these must be disabled or set to minimum.
Ray tracing options may need to be manually confirmed as Off in-game, as the remaster can enable some by default on first launch.
Shader compilation stutters are common on first traversal of new areas and should clear up after the initial play session.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Locked to 40 fps at 40 Hz for a smooth, tear-free feel that is noticeably more responsive than 30 fps; the GPU will run at full boost and the chip may sustain near 15 W, so expect heat and short battery life. Drop to Optimal if frame rate falls below 35 fps in Novigrad.
